family.tagline: Four people, one long table, one stair and one Companion Core.
family.story: Fernanda plans her lessons at the long table, and Chike works from the landing. Ayaan studies in Bedroom Two while Dmitri plays at the desk by the door. One Companion Core sits there too.

home.lede: A dark brick block on a city street, with white-railed walkways and a long flight of steps up to the first. The family's flat takes two floors of the middle bay, with a balcony over the back court.

spots.line: A tuxedo sofa, open shelves and the Core on its desk by the door.
A long oval table, a breakfast bar with stools and the balcony door.
A bistro table and two bentwood chairs over the back court.
A writing desk, a laptop and open shelves at the top of the stair.
A headboard bed and two lamps, with the stair a few paces away.

day.line: Fernanda writes the handout before the school run.
Chike checks his automations at the landing desk.
Someone checks the pantry before the shop.
Fernanda marks a batch in timed rounds.
Ayaan saves the articles for his history project.
Dmitri starts a Steam session at the desk.
Chike adds his weekend project's page to a watch list.
Dmitri puts a playlist on while he models.

companion.name: Clove
companion.job: Drafts reminders and letters for Fernanda's lessons from the context she connected.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Fernanda rewrites and sends every message.

profile.bio: Fernanda teaches secondary school and plans her lessons at the long table. Her handouts, diagrams and notes are files on the Core, and Clove drafts the letters she rewrites and sends herself.

companion.name: Cassia
companion.job: Opens the council's web forms and fills in the details Chike typed.
companion.limits: One form at a time. Chike reads each field and submits it himself.

profile.bio: Chike builds backend software for a team that works by video and keeps a weekend project on the landing desk. His repositories sit in Forgejo on the Core, and Cassia fills in the forms that he checks and submits himself.
Ayaan studies in Bedroom Two. He keeps his history notes with their sources, checks his German against the textbook and listens to his essays read back before he rewrites them.
Dmitri is in sixth form, plays Steam from the desk by the door and models in his spare time. His games, his models and his music all run on the Core.

popup.title: A parcel at the gallery door
popup.body: The courier leaves the parcel on the gallery, at the top of a long flight of steps. Chike carries it in through the door.

popup.title: Four things in the parcel
popup.body: Ayaan holds the parcel steady while Dmitri cuts the tape. Inside are the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive.

popup.title: Plugged in by the door
popup.body: Fernanda plugs the cable in at the desk by the front door. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from Chike's phone
popup.body: Chike joins the Core's own network from his phone, then picks the home network.

popup.title: Fernanda and Chike choose their agents
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Fernanda picks Hermes and Chike picks OpenClaw. Companion Memory comes along, with Donetick, Grocy and Forgejo. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Clove says hello
popup.body: Fernanda messages the agent she named Clove. The reply comes from the Core, on the desk by the door.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: fernanda
say.text: Hello, Fernanda. I am Clove. What should we start with?

detail.before: Without an agent, Fernanda wrote every reminder and letter herself, one app at a time.
detail.after: Clove runs in a sandbox on the Core and replies through the messaging app Fernanda picked. Those messages travel through that chat service.
steps: Pick Hermes in the Companion Hub store
Give the agent a name
Send it a first message
detail.fact: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: One install, two laptops
popup.body: Dmitri installs his games once, on the Core, and Steam runs there. On either laptop, he signs in with his Valve account and opens the session in a browser tab.
popup.note: Steam needs a Valve account. A Core may lack the graphics power a game wants.

detail.before: Every game was installed on each laptop that played it, and each laptop held its own copy of the downloads.
detail.after: Steam Headless holds the one install on the Core. Each laptop only opens the session in a browser tab, and Valve still keeps the account and the library.
steps: Install the game once on the Core
Sign in with his own Valve account
Open the session in a browser tab
detail.fact: Steam Headless runs Steam on your Core and plays it in a browser on a screen in the house.

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: Twelve years of lesson notes
popup.body: Twelve years of lesson notes now sit in Joplin Server on the Core. On Sunday Fernanda finds her first year's scheme of work and reuses it.
popup.note: Joplin Server is the server. The Joplin apps are separate.

detail.before: Twelve years of lesson notes sat in Evernote, one notebook for each year group.
detail.after: Joplin Server syncs the notes between her laptop and her phone through the server on the Core. The first year's scheme of work is still there.
steps: Import the old notebooks
Search for the first year's scheme
Copy it into this term's plan
detail.fact: Joplin Server lets you take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server.

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: A playlist for the modelling
popup.body: On the sofa, Dmitri plays the family's music files through Navidrome on the Core while he models. The playlist is a list of files, not an account.

detail.before: Dmitri's modelling playlists lived in Apple Music, apart from the songs the family already owned.
detail.after: Navidrome streams the music files on the Core to any device in the flat. His playlists sit beside the files they play.
steps: Open Navidrome in a browser
Pick songs from the music folder
Press play on the sofa
detail.fact: Navidrome streams your own music collection to any device.

beats.capability: model low-poly art in your browser

popup.title: A low-poly boat for coursework
popup.body: Dmitri models a low-poly boat for his design coursework in Blockbench, in a browser tab. The file sits in a folder on the Core.

detail.before: Dmitri's models lived in MagicaVoxel on one laptop, so each file stayed where he had made it.
detail.after: Blockbench opens in a browser tab served by the Core. He builds the boat there, and every laptop in the flat opens the same file.
steps: Open Blockbench in a browser tab
Build the boat from blocks
Save the model to the coursework folder
detail.fact: Blockbench models low-poly art in your browser.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: The new router asks the Core
popup.body: The provider swaps the flat's router on Tuesday. Chike points its DNS setting at the Core, and Pi-hole answers the flat's lookups again.
popup.note: Lookups it does not block still go to the DNS provider the family picked.

detail.before: The flat's DNS filter was a NextDNS profile, and the new router did not carry it over.
detail.after: Pi-hole answers the flat's DNS from the Core. Chike sets the router to ask the Core, and every device follows it.
steps: Open the new router's settings
Set its DNS to the Core
Check that a blocked ad domain stays blocked
detail.fact: Pi-hole blocks ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level.

beats.capability: the LibreOffice suite, Writer, Calc and more, in your browser

popup.title: Thursday's handout, written at the table
popup.body: Fernanda writes Thursday's handout at the long table. LibreOffice opens in a browser tab from the Core, and the file lands in her lesson folder there.

detail.before: Fernanda wrote her handouts in Google Workspace, and each one lived in that account.
detail.after: LibreOffice runs in a browser tab from the Core. Her handouts are files in a lesson folder on the Core, one for each week.
steps: Open LibreOffice in a browser tab
Write the handout at the table
Save it to the lesson folder
detail.fact: The LibreOffice suite, Writer, Calc and more, runs in your browser.

beats.capability: a whiteboard with a hand-drawn look to sketch ideas together

popup.title: Friday's diagram, sketched at the table
popup.body: Fernanda sketches the water cycle for Friday's lesson in Excalidraw. The board opens in her browser from the Core, and she keeps the drawing beside the handout.

detail.before: Fernanda sketched her lesson diagrams on Miro boards, and the boards stayed there.
detail.after: Excalidraw opens in her browser from the Core. She sketches the diagram with its hand-drawn look and saves it in the lesson folder.
steps: Open a fresh board in Excalidraw
Sketch the water cycle
Save the drawing beside the handout
detail.fact: Excalidraw is a whiteboard with a hand-drawn look. Sketch ideas together.

beats.capability: plan your day, track time and run a Pomodoro timer

popup.title: Marking in timed rounds
popup.body: Fernanda marks the class's essays in Super Productivity on the Core, one timed round for each batch of five. The timer runs, and the breaks are on the list.

detail.before: Marking ran on in long stretches, and the to-do list lived in Todoist apart from the timer.
detail.after: Super Productivity keeps the marking list and a Pomodoro timer together on the Core, so each round starts with the next batch.
steps: Add a task for each batch
Start the timer for the round
Take the break when it ends
detail.fact: Super Productivity helps you plan your day, track time and run a Pomodoro timer.

beats.capability: keeps your digital life on your own disk and gives your agents individual context

popup.title: Clove drafts, Fernanda rewrites
popup.body: Clove drafts the trip reminder from last year's letter, which Fernanda connected to Companion Memory. She rewrites it in her own words, then sends it herself.

detail.before: A trip reminder meant digging out last year's letter and retyping the dates.
detail.after: Clove drafts the reminder on the Core from the letter Fernanda connected in Companion Memory. She rewrites it and sends it herself.
steps: Ask Clove for the trip reminder
Check the dates against the trip sheet
Rewrite it and send it herself
detail.fact: Companion Memory keeps your digital life on your disk, so your agents know your context.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: Sunday's shop starts at the fridge
popup.body: The pantry stock and the shopping list sit in Grocy on the Core. Before the Sunday shop, the family checks the fridge against the list.

detail.before: The list lived in OurGroceries, with no record of what was already in the cupboards.
detail.after: Grocy keeps the pantry stock and the list on the Core, so the list shows only what is running low.
steps: Count the tins and the rice
Add what is running low
Read the list at the shop
detail.fact: Grocy tracks the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place.

beats.capability: assign and track household chores and recurring tasks

popup.title: The bins rota has four names
popup.body: Donetick sets the week for four people, from the bins to the balcony. Each chore is ticked off on the Core when it is done.
popup.note: Reminders pass through an outside notification service.

detail.before: The week's chores lived in Tody, and whose turn it was depended on which phone you asked.
detail.after: Donetick keeps the rota on the Core. It assigns each chore, repeats it, and shows whose turn is next.
steps: Add the weekly chores
Give each one a name and a day
Tick a chore off when it is done
detail.fact: Donetick assigns and tracks household chores and recurring tasks.

beats.capability: watch your sites and services and get an alert when one goes down

popup.title: The weekend project, watched
popup.body: On the balcony, Chike adds his weekend project's test page to Uptime Kuma on the Core. If the page stops answering, he hears about it first.

detail.before: The weekend project's page had no check, and Chike learned it was down from a tester's message.
detail.after: Uptime Kuma checks the page every few minutes from the Core, and Chike hears about a failure before his testers do.
steps: Add the test page as a check
Pick who gets the alert
Read the history after a deploy
detail.fact: Uptime Kuma watches your sites and services and sends an alert when one goes down.

beats.capability: manage and read books, comics and PDFs with automatic covers and metadata

popup.title: The set text reads outside
popup.body: The school sends the set text as a file. Ayaan adds it to BookLore, which fetches the cover from outside, and reads it on the balcony.
popup.note: BookLore fetches covers and details from outside.

detail.before: Ayaan read his set texts in Apple Books, with his place kept in that app.
detail.after: BookLore keeps the school's file in a library on the Core and remembers his page. Only the cover and book details come from outside.
steps: Add the school's file to the library
Open it from the Core
Pick up at the page he left
detail.fact: BookLore manages and reads books, comics and PDFs with automatic covers and metadata.

beats.capability: host your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core

popup.title: A weekend project gets a home
popup.body: Chike pushes his weekend project, a bus-timetable board, to Forgejo on the Core. Its issues and pull requests sit beside the code.

detail.before: Chike kept his weekend projects on GitLab, with their issues and merge requests there too.
detail.after: Forgejo hosts the repository on the Core, with its issues and pull requests beside it.
steps: Point the repository at Forgejo
Push the timetable branch
Open the pull request on the Core
detail.fact: Forgejo hosts your own Git repositories, issues and pull requests on your Core.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows

popup.title: Three automations move to the Core
popup.body: Chike moves three small automations out of a rented service and into n8n. They run on the Core and pass data between the apps he installed.

detail.before: Chike built his small automations in Zapier, one rented step after another.
detail.after: n8n runs the same workflows on the Core. The data they pass between his installed apps stays on the Core.
steps: Rebuild the first workflow in n8n
Connect it to an installed app
Run it once and read the result
detail.fact: n8n connects your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Cassia fills in the permit form
popup.body: Cassia opens the council's parking page and fills in the renewal form for the flat's bay. Chike checks every field, then submits it himself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: chike
say.text: The renewal form is filled in. Please check the vehicle details before you submit it.

detail.before: Renewing the parking permit meant typing the same details into the council's form each year.
detail.after: Cassia opens the council's page in its browser and fills in the form from what Chike typed. Chike reads every field and submits it himself.
steps: Type the bay and the vehicle details
Let Cassia fill in the form
Read every field, then submit it

beats.capability: save articles to read later without a hosted bookmarking service

popup.title: Articles kept for the project
popup.body: Ayaan saves the articles for his history project in Readeck on the Core. Each one is kept as a clean copy he can read at his desk.

detail.before: Ayaan saved articles to Instapaper, and the only copy lived in that account.
detail.after: Readeck keeps each article as a copy on the Core, so it opens at his desk even if the page changes.
steps: Save the article in Readeck
Tag it with the topic
Open the copy when he writes the essay
detail.fact: Readeck saves articles to read later without a hosted bookmarking service.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: One sentence, checked twice
popup.body: Ayaan translates a German sentence both ways in LibreTranslate, then checks it against his textbook. The Core runs the translator, and the textbook has the last word.

detail.before: Ayaan checked his German sentences in DeepL, one pasted line at a time.
detail.after: LibreTranslate runs on the Core. Ayaan translates a sentence both ways, then checks it against his textbook before he writes it down.
steps: Type the German sentence
Translate it both ways
Check the result against the textbook
detail.fact: LibreTranslate translates text and documents on your own Core.

beats.capability: turn text into natural speech on your own Core

popup.title: The essay, read back to him
popup.body: Ayaan pastes his essay into Kokoro and listens to it read aloud. The sentences that drag stand out when he hears them, and he rewrites them himself.

detail.before: Ayaan read his essay through once and never noticed where the sentences dragged.
detail.after: Kokoro turns the essay into speech on the Core. Ayaan hears the clumsy lines, marks them and rewrites them himself.
steps: Paste the essay into Kokoro
Listen and mark the clumsy lines
Rewrite them by hand
detail.fact: Kokoro turns text into speech on your own Core.

beats.capability: split shared costs and settle up with the fewest payments

popup.title: Two brothers split a present
popup.body: Dmitri adds the cost of their mother's birthday present to Spliit, and Ayaan's share comes out. It works out who owes whom and does not move money.

detail.before: Dmitri and Ayaan kept their shared costs in Splitwise, and the tally lived with that service.
detail.after: Spliit keeps the tally on the Core. Each present is one entry, and the app works out who owes whom.
steps: Add the present as one cost
Pick Ayaan's share
Settle up when they have paid
detail.fact: Spliit splits shared costs and settles up with the fewest payments.

popup.title: One flat, four different days
popup.body: A teacher's table, a developer's landing, two brothers' rooms and one Companion Core by the door.

closing.body: A teacher's lessons, a developer's repositories and two teenagers' schoolwork can live on a Companion Core. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: Told in the v3 shape: 16 of 20 room beats are pairs. The four pair-less ones are the Companion Memory draft, the OpenClaw permit form, Kokoro reading an essay back and Dmitri's Steam Headless session.
The file is rademaker.json because the slug is the family's (cast plan: rademaker lives in the home with the long table); the home is the walkup-duplex apartment.

Steam Headless is pair-less on purpose, as in the Voss flat: its only pairs are cloud gaming services, which the copy lint refuses by name. The persona-replaces warning on living-session is that choice.
Age rule 16: Ayaan (13) and Dmitri (16) use no chat model or agent in their own beats; Clove and Cassia work only for Fernanda and Chike, who approve every result.

Honest edges carried: Steam needs a Valve account; Pi-hole forwards unblocked lookups to the family DNS provider; Donetick reminders use an outside notification service; BookLore fetches covers from outside; Spliit does not move money.
The home has no TV: the media beat at the couch is Dmitri's Navidrome playlist; he plays Steam in a browser tab at the desk by the door.
No third-party app is in more than two of the six apartments: Uptime Kuma, Super Productivity, Navidrome and Readeck are this flat's.
